threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Word document engine exposed as a Rust library/native CLI, PyO3 Python library/CLI and stdio MCP server, and wasm-bindgen Node/browser APIs with a Node CLI. It accepts DOCX, supported legacy DOC and Markdown, then compares, inspects, edits, resolves revisions, renders and exports byte documents (README.md:29-42; src/lib.rs:15-30; jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:43-49; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:7-28). Native hosts additionally provide filesystem authority, font discovery/cache persistence and publication. Self-update downloads fixed GitHub release assets and replaces the executable (src/update.rs:186-258); tag CI and operator release scripts publish distributions using separate credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,230-235,356-369; scripts/release.sh:907-959). No deployment context or supplied authoritative model exists.
assets: Document contents, comments, authorship, revision history, media and exported Markdown/JSON/PDF/PNG, including confidential views/reports (README.md:32-42; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,185-218).
Source-bound edit integrity: legacy plans optionally guard source SHA-256; V2 requires matching source.sha256 before resolution (src/edit.rs:2081-2089; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-111).

Native filesystem and output integrity: MCP explicit document/output I/O uses held OutputRoot; native CLI publication grants ambient selected local paths (jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-218).

Embedding application/browser/CLI CPU and memory: default admission 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB inflated, 10,000 entries and depth 256; comparison 512 MiB compressed/per-part, 2 GiB inflated with same entry/depth caps (src/admission.rs:63-99).

Native font files and persistent font-index paths/stamps, whose host-environment-derived location and temporary sibling are independent of document output roots (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3106,3154-3168,3183-3229).

Installed executable, release assets, crate/npm/PyPI distributions and conditional signing-key authority (src/update.rs:25-48,198-258; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-310,356-369; scripts/release.sh:907-959,1042-1067).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted document producer -> in-process parser/comparer/renderer. Admission checks package budgets; shared production archive open checks structural defects. Debug deliberately uses unchecked archive open for triage. Engine controls differ from host CPU/memory obligations (src/admission.rs:13-28,63-99; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778).

Edit-plan producer -> mutation: V2 validates plan, required hash, scope/context and maps operations; legacy source binding is conditional on source_sha256 being present (src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-111; src/edit.rs:2073-2094).

MCP client -> operator-granted root. --root or cwd resolves and opens native OutputRoot once. Inputs/outputs pass relative names through held cap_std handles; Python containment is diagnostic. ToolAnnotations are hints, not separate caller authorization/approval (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108,152-159,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199).

MCP/native rendering -> ambient fonts/cache: docx_render and optional edit rendering load font resources outside explicit document/output capability. Index path is JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX (empty/off disables), else parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv; user_font_dir is JUBARTE_FONT_DIR when nonempty, else macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts. Temporary sibling replaces extension with tsv.<pid>.tmp. Readers are later native processes/local filesystem users; control is host permissions and index version/stamps, not MCP OutputRoot (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-191,234-255; src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3112,3154-3168,3183-3229).

Native renderer -> system/Word font discovery: macOS /System/Library/Fonts[/Supplemental], /Library/Fonts[/Microsoft], /Applications/Microsoft Word.app/Contents/Resources/DFonts; Windows WINDIR/SystemRoot/default C:\Windows plus Fonts and LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts; macOS Word cloud $HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family> with one-normal-component family constraint. Host environment/permissions own these resources; font bytes reach parser/shaper/outputs (src/convert/font.rs:2228-2235,2281-2315,2855-2862).

Local CLI operator -> ambient files: Rust opens selected parent once, stages .jubarte-<UUID>.partial with Unix mode 0700, verifies all bytes and commits per file. Python/Node wrappers directly read/write selected paths under OS authority; no MCP confinement is implied (src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:100-130,203-218,440-495; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:61-89,101-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-111).

MCP exports -> root filesystem readers: edit writes fixed clean.docx/redline.docx/patch.diff/report.json plus optional redline.pdf/redline-page-NN.png below out_dir; render writes page-NN.png and optional render.pdf. overwrite defaults false, native OutputRoot validates names/stages all bytes, but each file commits independently. Responses expose paths/report/text/font information, not document bytes as export payloads (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:152-255; src/publication.rs:100-130,175-199).

Markdown image references -> native local reads. --resource-path wins, else Markdown parent or '.', canonicalized and held as directory capability; percent-decoding precedes URL rejection, containment and capability-relative reads. Image bytes enter generated DOCX/output. Python/Node reject unsupported resource-path rather than inheriting native resource authority (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2876,2936-2943; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1058-1062; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-726).

Browser/Node caller -> WASM byte API: host supplies/receives bytes or JSON, native publication is excluded on wasm32; Node CLI separately adds filesystem authority (jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:7-28; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-79,106-111).

GitHub release authority -> installed executable. Explicit self-update selects fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines and platform, latest/requested version, binary member jubarte-<version>-<platform>/jubarte[.exe], SHA256SUMS.txt, confirmation/--yes and regular-file verifier. Current RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean checksum-only; signatures are conditional support (src/update.rs:25-48,83-108,186-258,299-310; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80).

Maintainer/tag authority -> publication. v* CI checks version/tag match, read-only build jobs, contents:write release job. Step-scoped ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY is decoded to $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN, cleanup trap, 64-byte length/committed-public-key checks, signatures before checksums. Missing secret fails only if public keys exist. GH_TOKEN references GITHUB_TOKEN for publishing dist/* to github.repository release ( .github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,40-49,230-321,356-369).

Operator registry authority -> crates.io jubarte-redlines, npm jubarte-wasm then jubarte-redlines, PyPI dist/pypi wheel/sdist sets. Local registry credentials, optional npm OTP, packaged-summary/complete-wheel-set checks apply; --no-wait explicitly consents to local partial platform set (scripts/release.sh:907-959,1042-1067).
attackerCapabilities: Document suppliers control malformed DOCX/XML/media/fonts/Markdown and image references; host environment, root grants, release credentials and installation remain outside this capability (src/admission.rs:13-28; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2876).

MCP clients invoke exposed read/edit/render/compare/revision tools and may request overwrite=true under granted root; no independent caller role or human-approval gate is established (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-159,258-327).
Library callers may override InputLimits, including raising them; this is already their embedding configuration authority (src/admission.rs:103-165).
CLI/harness callers choose paths under existing OS authority; no new isolation is inferred (src/publication.rs:203-218; jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:91-99).

Release asset control affects updater inputs; checksum-only verification depends on release hosting trust, distinct from document submission or compiled signing keys (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:25-48,245-257).
securityObjectives: Reject unsupported, inconsistent and over-budget packages before unrestricted downstream inflation/parsing, while retaining the diagnostic debug exception (src/admission.rs:13-28,63-99; src/opc/archive.rs:15-51).

Confine explicit MCP reads/exports to startup directory capability, portable relative output names and overwrite policy (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108; src/publication.rs:146-199,440-463).

Enforce promised source hash/scope/context binding and refuse invalid plans before document publication (src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-111; src/edit.rs:2081-2089; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:170-217).
Stage/verify all native outputs before first commit and report partial commits/durability failures honestly, without promising global atomicity (src/publication.rs:100-130,168-174).
Keep Markdown images within native resource capability and prohibit URL fetches (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2835-2876,2936-2943).

Reserve executable replacement for explicit update with fixed asset/checksum/configured-signature controls; scope signing/release secrets to privileged consumers and protect confidential reports (src/update.rs:25-48,186-258; .github/workflows/release.yml:261-310; SECURITY.md:12-35).
assumptions: Exact userContext=null; no supplied model, source inventory or KB. Remote uploads, multi-tenant service and hostile MCP clients are deployment conditions, not established HTTP/authentication surfaces.

Root SECURITY.md is the sole inherited security policy, covers engine/CLI/bindings, requires caller CPU/memory limits and distinguishes supported signatures from actual checksum-only releases (SECURITY.md:7-9,65-80).

Documentation discrepancy: src/lib.rs:7-11 says byte APIs use no temporary files, but native font index persists/stages a sibling file; MCP build_server says tools only touch root yet transitive font operations use ambient paths (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-68; src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3106,3183-3229). No attacker-controlled index path or exploitable cache disclosure is established.
Current empty compiled keys/threshold agree with staged-signing docs; dependency/CI signature capability does not mean enforced signing (src/update.rs:44-48,245-249; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69-80).
docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 advertises GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN support but src/update.rs:198-210 does not explicitly configure a token; dependency credential lookup/recipient behavior remains unverified.
Publication is per-file, not an atomic set; Windows directory sync is deliberately a no-op, without an established authorization failure (src/publication.rs:100-130,168-174,387-405).
The benchmark worker is stdin/stdout developer tooling with ambient paths, not evidence of a network service (jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:5-20,91-99).

Actual host/root/env permissions, deployed client exposure and registry/release approval settings are unknown. Review is offline static; no application execution, crafted-input execution, network or source changes.

findings.title: Rendering an embedded HTML table can exhaust memory
findings.summary: A document-controlled HTML `colspan` is expanded into that many WordprocessingML grid columns before layout. A tiny admitted DOCX can request billions of columns and exhaust the renderer process or WASM instance.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reliably force unbounded generated allocation during rendering. Impact is availability of the processing host; no code execution or data access is established.
severity.changeConditions: Risk is reduced by strict process memory/CPU isolation; a shared long-lived conversion service increases affected availability.

confidence.rationale: Static trace connects the public renderer to unbounded `usize` colspan parsing and the proportional String-writing loop; no intervening cap exists.

codeEvidence.label: Render expands admitted HTML before parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: The renderer loads package-controlled chunk bytes and calls the HTML expander after input admission.

codeEvidence.label: HTML colspan has no upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: Any parsed usize is retained; max(1) enforces only a minimum, so a short attribute can request billions of columns.

codeEvidence.label: Cell spans determine generated column count
codeEvidence.code:
let cols = table
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.iter().map(|c| c.span).sum::<usize>())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        let col_w = 9360 / cols;
codeEvidence.explanation: A single large span becomes cols without a resource bound. One large cell avoids any need for sum overflow.

codeEvidence.label: Each requested column grows an output String
codeEvidence.explanation: The loop allocates output proportional to the attacker numeric value rather than input size, exhausting memory before downstream layout validation.

rootCause.summary: `with_layout()` admits the package, then expands its HTML altChunk. `Builder::start()` parses `colspan` into `usize` and only enforces a minimum. `end_table()` uses the span sum as `cols` and appends a grid element once per column without bounding generated output.

findings.remediation: Reject HTML table spans and cumulative grid sizes above a documented supported limit using checked arithmetic, and enforce a generated-output budget before appending grid cells.

counterEvidence: Input admission bounds archive bytes/entries/depth and callers are advised to impose CPU/memory limits; neither limits HTML colspan or generated grid size.
The effect requires rendering an attacker-supplied document; no remote service deployment was assumed.
limitations: No application execution or runtime exploit was performed.
validation.summary: Public PDF and render-report APIs reach `with_layout()`, which expands HTML from a local package relationship. A one-cell table with a very large valid `colspan` reaches `0..cols` before DOM/layout checks. ZIP byte, entry, and XML-depth budgets cannot bound this numeric expansion.

dataflow.summary: DOCX HTML part -> `altchunk::expand()` -> `html_to_wml()` -> parsed cell span -> `end_table()` -> proportional grid String allocation.

impact.why: Availability loss of the processing host or instance.

likelihood.why: Small input directly controls an unbounded loop/allocation.

reachability.summary: A supplier controls document bytes; the victim invokes a public rendering API. No privileged configuration, external relationship fetching, or raised input limits is needed.

attackPath.summary: Supply a valid DOCX with a main-document `w:altChunk` relationship to HTML containing one table cell and a huge `colspan`, then have the recipient render PDF/PNG or obtain a render report.

remediationTests: A one-cell HTML table with an excessive numeric colspan returns a typed refusal without allocating proportional output.
Multiple spans cannot overflow the cumulative count or bypass the generated-grid limit.
Ordinary bounded colspan tables retain rendering behavior.

findings.title: Comparing documents can bypass XML depth limits through renamed note parts
findings.summary: Admission selects XML policy by filename suffix, but the comparator resolves footnote/endnote XML by relationships regardless of suffix. A deeply nested notes part named `.bin` reaches the unchecked recursive DOM parser and can terminate the embedding process with stack exhaustion.

severity.rationale: A document producer can bypass an explicit parser depth control and deny availability during comparison; no code execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Process isolation reduces collateral impact; using checked XML APIs for every semantic XML consumer closes this path.

confidence.rationale: Static trace confirms suffix-only admission, relationship-based auxiliary loading and direct unbounded recursive parsing before note semantics are inspected.

codeEvidence.label: Admission recognizes XML only by extension
codeEvidence.explanation: An auxiliary part with another extension is counted as bytes but skips check_xml_depth and its tag policy; the subsequent fallback only checks the main document.

codeEvidence.label: Notes are located by relationship type
codeEvidence.explanation: The document supplier chooses an internal notes target such as word/notes.bin; no extension constraint is applied.

codeEvidence.label: Resolved notes use unchecked DOM parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: Both notes paths parse fetched text before validating semantic contents, without a checked XML gate carrying InputLimits.

codeEvidence.label: DOM descent consumes one stack frame per element
codeEvidence.explanation: Unchecked parsing recursively handles nested elements without a depth counter, so a short but deeply nested XML payload can exhaust the process/instance stack.

rootCause.summary: Admission gates XML depth/tag checks on `.xml`/`.rels` suffixes and only adds a main-part fallback. Comparator preprocessing instead trusts relationship types to identify notes, loads their text regardless of name and invokes unchecked recursive `parse_xdocument()`. Semantic XML consumers therefore receive unbounded nesting despite successful package admission.

findings.remediation: Apply active XML limits at every semantic XML parse boundary, including relationship-resolved notes, or enumerate XML parts by content types and relationship consumers before parsing. Use checked DOM APIs in comparator preprocessing.

counterEvidence: `.xml`/`.rels` parts and the main document are depth/tag checked, and inspect has checked XML paths; those controls do not cover this relationship-resolved comparator path.
ZIP byte/entry/inflated limits still apply, but tens of thousands of nested tags fit comfortably within defaults.
The infallible raw DOM API is documented as unchecked; the report concerns its use after incomplete package admission, not the existence of that API.
limitations: No runtime stack-overflow reproduction; exact failing depth depends on host stack and target.
validation.summary: Compared nonidentical packages are admitted, opened, then passed to pre_process_markup. An internal footnotes/endnotes relationship can name a safe `.bin` part with an XML content-type override; PartFs stores/returns it without adding an XML-depth check. The note parser runs before note-reference/shape handling, reaching recursive descent.

dataflow.summary: Relationship-controlled non-.xml part -> byte-only admission -> pre_process_markup -> unchecked DOM recursion.

likelihood.why: Filename selection deterministically bypasses the explicit XML gate.

reachability.summary: Public comparison accepts producer-controlled packages and preprocesses semantic note targets without requiring privileged configuration or raised limits.
reachability.outcome: Embedding process or WASM instance loses availability
preconditions: Comparison processes a nonidentical input pair containing the crafted notes relationship.

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with a normal shallow main part and a footnotes/endnotes relationship to deeply nested XML under a `.bin` name; have it compared with a different document.

remediationTests: A deeply nested footnotes/endnotes part named notes.bin receives the same INVALID_XML refusal as notes.xml.
Custom-named auxiliary XML also honors attribute/tag budgets under active InputLimits.
Ordinary valid custom-named notes continue to compare.

findings.title: Rendering a huge tab stop can panic or exhaust memory
findings.summary: A short paragraph with an oversized left tab stop and a dot/hyphen/underscore leader reaches a destination-derived `String::repeat()` without a range or output-length check.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can cause disproportionate CPU/memory consumption in the processing host. Availability impact is medium and the direct input path has high likelihood; no execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Per-job CPU/memory isolation limits collateral impact; shared long-lived service deployment increases affected availability.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source inspection confirms input parsing, propagation, missing work/allocation bound and reachable sink. Runtime duration/host failure was not measured.

codeEvidence.label: Tab positions accept unbounded floats
codeEvidence.explanation: `w:pos` is parsed as f32 and converted from twips without finite/magnitude bounds; attacker-selected leader and alignment are retained.

codeEvidence.label: Only modern right-aligned stops are clamped
codeEvidence.explanation: A huge left tab stop survives the only shown margin clamp.

codeEvidence.label: Unchecked destination reaches leader painter
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected leader sends the computed tab destination to `paint_tab_leader()`.

codeEvidence.label: Leader distance becomes repeated allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: Float-derived character count becomes usize and controls String::repeat without checked allocation or visible-interval bound.

rootCause.summary: `parse_tab_stops()` retains an arbitrarily large floating position. Layout preserves left stops, and a lone explicit tab survives wrapping. `advance_tab()` passes its distant endpoint to `paint_tab_leader()`, which casts the calculated count to usize and repeats a marker.

findings.remediation: Require finite supported tab positions, clip leaders to a bounded visible interval, and reject repeated-text allocations beyond a checked per-render budget.

counterEvidence: Admission bounds source ZIP/XML size, nesting and entries, and the policy recommends host process limits. These do not bound this generated work.
Modern right-aligned tab clamping does not cover the left-aligned trigger; raster pixel limits are downstream.
limitations: No application execution or vulnerability-triggering runtime test was performed.
validation.summary: Reviewed public `with_layout()` admission, paragraph tab application, lone-tab wrapping and paint path. A finite position such as 1e30 twips exceeds addressable repeated text; the count cast saturates and repeat can panic, while smaller huge values allocate excessive memory.

dataflow.summary: `parse_tab_stops()` retains an arbitrarily large floating position. Layout preserves left stops, and a lone explicit tab survives wrapping. `advance_tab()` passes its distant endpoint to `paint_tab_leader()`, which casts the calculated count to usize and repeats a marker.

impact.why: Availability of the conversion/comparison process or instance.

likelihood.why: The input directly selects excessive work with no required privileged configuration.

reachability.summary: The public renderer accepts attacker-supplied document bytes and reaches this path with default input budgets.
reachability.outcome: Conversion worker consumes excessive resources or fails

attackPath.summary: Render a DOCX containing a paragraph with one explicit left tab stop, a very large numeric `w:pos`, a dot leader, and an actual tab run.

remediationTests: Huge finite, nonfinite and negative tab positions return a typed refusal or bounded rendering.
Exercise left/center/decimal and legacy right tabs; downstream raster limits must not be the first guard.

originalCandidate.originalEvidence: parse_tab_stops:3243 parses unbounded f32 pos; advance_tab:26447-26469 passes destination to paint_tab_leader:26393-26400, which casts count to usize and mark.repeat(n). landed_tab_stops:24141-24154 clamps right stops only with compat>=15; left/center/decimal remain. Lone-tab wrapping reachability pending.

findings.title: Rendering a long paragraph performs quadratic suffix scans
findings.summary: Wrapping computes every remaining token suffix before line breaking, even when the paragraph contains no tabs and does not need suffix widths.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can cause disproportionate CPU/memory consumption in the processing host. Availability impact is medium and the direct input path has high likelihood; no execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Per-job CPU/memory isolation limits collateral impact; shared long-lived service deployment increases affected availability.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source inspection confirms input parsing, propagation, missing work/allocation bound and reachable sink. Runtime duration/host failure was not measured.

codeEvidence.label: Words and spaces become separate units
codeEvidence.explanation: Whitespace boundaries produce many units from a short repeated-word paragraph.

codeEvidence.label: Every unit scans its whole suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: Without tabs, each suffix scan reaches the end; N units cause N*(N-1)/2 visits before wrapping.

rootCause.summary: Paragraph runs become word/space units. `wrap_runs_segment()` unconditionally builds `tails` by summing `units[i+1..]` for every i, stopping only at tabs. A tab-free paragraph therefore pays quadratic work for widths that will never be used.

findings.remediation: Compute suffix widths in a single reverse pass with resets at tab boundaries, or skip suffix work for tab-free segments.

counterEvidence: Admission bounds source ZIP/XML size, nesting and entries, and the policy recommends host process limits. These do not bound this generated work.
limitations: No application execution or vulnerability-triggering runtime test was performed.
validation.summary: Checked token splitting, unit construction and wrapping dispatch. Ordinary repeated words separated by single spaces form linearly many units, no explicit line breaks split the segment, and every suffix reaches the end. Byte budgets allow far more units than a practical quadratic scan can process.

dataflow.summary: Paragraph runs become word/space units. `wrap_runs_segment()` unconditionally builds `tails` by summing `units[i+1..]` for every i, stopping only at tabs. A tab-free paragraph therefore pays quadratic work for widths that will never be used.
dataflow.sink: Every unit scans its whole suffix

reachability.outcome: Conversion worker consumes excessive resources or fails

attackPath.summary: Render a document with one long tab-free paragraph containing many space-separated short words. Hundreds of thousands of units imply tens of billions of suffix visits before layout can finish.

remediationTests: A large no-tab paragraph performs a linear number of suffix-width operations.
Center/right tab alignment retains correct suffix widths across consecutive tabs and explicit breaks.

findings.title: Rendering a Chicago list marker can allocate gigabytes
findings.summary: A one-item Chicago-format list with a large start or startOverride expands its numeric counter into proportional marker text; the largest u32 requests about 3 GiB.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can cause disproportionate CPU/memory consumption in the processing host. Availability impact is medium and the direct input path has high likelihood; no execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Per-job CPU/memory isolation limits collateral impact; shared long-lived service deployment increases affected availability.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source inspection confirms input parsing, propagation, missing work/allocation bound and reachable sink. Runtime duration/host failure was not measured.

codeEvidence.label: List start accepts u32 without output bound
codeEvidence.explanation: The parsed start value reaches the numbering definition.

codeEvidence.label: Instance overrides retain the same unchecked start
codeEvidence.explanation: An instance startOverride is a second input route to the same counter.

codeEvidence.label: Counter preserves the supplied start
codeEvidence.code:
let start = self
            .starts
            .get(&(num_id.to_string(), resolved))
            .copied()
            .unwrap_or(lvl.start)
            .max(1);
        let cur = *self
            .counters
            .entry((num_id.to_string(), resolved))
            .or_insert(start);
        self.counters
            .insert((num_id.to_string(), resolved), cur.saturating_add(1));
        self.render(&abs, num_id, resolved, &lvl, cur)
codeEvidence.explanation: Only a lower bound is applied before the counter is rendered.

codeEvidence.label: Chicago format selects the repeat formatter
codeEvidence.code:
fn format_num(fmt: NumFmt, n: u32) -> String {
    match fmt {
        NumFmt::Decimal => n.to_string(),
        NumFmt::DecimalZero => format!("{n:02}"),
        NumFmt::CardinalText => cardinal_label(n),
        NumFmt::Ordinal => ordinal_label(n),
        NumFmt::OrdinalText => ordinal_text_label(n),
        NumFmt::Hex => format!("{n:X}"),
        NumFmt::Chicago => chicago_label(n),
codeEvidence.explanation: The active numbering format reaches chicago_label.

codeEvidence.label: Counter becomes proportional marker text
codeEvidence.explanation: The maximum u32 yields 1,073,741,824 copies of a three-byte double dagger before later copies/layout.

rootCause.summary: Numbering start/startOverride values enter u32 counters with only max(1). `Numbering::render()` calls `format_num()`, whose Chicago branch repeats one marker `(n-1)/4+1` times without an output budget.

findings.remediation: Bound rendered Chicago marker length and generated numbering bytes; return a typed refusal or a documented bounded fallback for excessive counters.

counterEvidence: Admission bounds source ZIP/XML size, nesting and entries, and the policy recommends host process limits. These do not bound this generated work.
limitations: No application execution or vulnerability-triggering runtime test was performed.
validation.summary: Verified initial counter selection, render formatting and repeat arithmetic. A start of 4294967295 selects the double-dagger marker and requests 3,221,225,472 UTF-8 bytes. XML size and depth remain small; source byte limits cannot prevent the allocation.

dataflow.summary: Numbering start/startOverride values enter u32 counters with only max(1). `Numbering::render()` calls `format_num()`, whose Chicago branch repeats one marker `(n-1)/4+1` times without an output budget.

impact.why: Availability of the conversion/comparison process or instance.

likelihood.why: The input directly selects excessive work with no required privileged configuration.

reachability.outcome: Conversion worker consumes excessive resources or fails

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX numbering definition using Chicago format with a huge start (or instance startOverride), and a paragraph that references it, then render.

findings.title: Rendering an undefined list level can perform billions of lookups
findings.summary: A document can set `w:ilvl` to an arbitrary u32. Resolving an undefined level iterates every smaller integer rather than the small set of defined levels.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can cause disproportionate CPU/memory consumption in the processing host. Availability impact is medium and the direct input path has high likelihood; no execution or disclosure is established.
severity.changeConditions: Per-job CPU/memory isolation limits collateral impact; shared long-lived service deployment increases affected availability.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source inspection confirms input parsing, propagation, missing work/allocation bound and reachable sink. Runtime duration/host failure was not measured.

codeEvidence.label: Numbering resolves the supplied level
codeEvidence.explanation: next_marker passes the value to resolve_ilvl before generating a marker.

codeEvidence.label: Fallback iterates the numeric range
codeEvidence.explanation: With only level zero defined, ilvl=4294967295 forces roughly 4.3 billion map probes.

rootCause.summary: `num_pr()` parses unbounded u32 `ilvl`. Numbering fallback uses `(0..ilvl).rev().find(...)` to locate a lower defined level. Work scales with attacker-selected identifier magnitude rather than the number of actual definitions.

findings.remediation: Reject unsupported levels and choose the greatest defined lower level by inspecting actual defined keys, with work bounded by the definition count.

counterEvidence: Admission bounds source ZIP/XML size, nesting and entries, and the policy recommends host process limits. These do not bound this generated work.
limitations: No application execution or vulnerability-triggering runtime test was performed.
validation.summary: Traced paragraph numPr through list_marker/next_revised/next_marker to resolve_ilvl. A normal abstract list defining only level zero and a huge undefined requested level avoids the exact-key fast path and forces the reverse-range scan.
